papers.title: LUNA-FM: a subword foundation model for long non-coding RNAs for functional inference.
papers.abstract: RNA foundation models (FMs) have shown promise for RNA identification and functional annotation. However, many use single-nucleotide tokenization, which produces long input sequences and can increase computational costs when modelling long RNAs, including long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs). To address these limitations, we introduce LUNA-FM (Length-efficient sUbword-based Nucleic Acid Foundation Model), an RNA language model pretrained on approximately 28 million redundancy-filtered ncRNA sequences. LUNA-FM combines subword tokenization with a long context transformer, enabling efficient modelling
papers.summary: LUNA-FM is a new RNA foundation model that uses subword tokenization instead of single-nucleotide tokenization, allowing it to process long non-coding RNAs more efficiently. Pretrained on ~28 million non-coding RNA sequences, it combines subword tokenization with a long-context transformer for functional inference. This reduces computational costs for modeling long RNAs while maintaining performance.

papers.title: Natural Language Processing Supported by Annotation Process Artifacts to Detect Risky Alcohol Use in Electronic Health Records: Algorithm Development and Validation Study.
papers.abstract: High-risk alcohol use and alcohol use disorder (AUD) are significant contributors to surgical risk and complications yet remain underidentified in surgical populations. While electronic health records (EHRs) contain relevant information about patients' alcohol use in clinical notes, manual chart review is time-intensive and impractical at scale. Natural language processing (NLP) offers a path to automated identification, but alcohol-related risk classes are highly imbalanced in clinical populations, making multiclass classification particularly challenging.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates a natural language processing (NLP) approach that leverages annotation process artifacts to detect risky alcohol use in electronic health records, addressing the challenge of highly imbalanced multiclass classification in surgical populations. The work aims to improve automated identification of high-risk alcohol use and alcohol use disorder, which are underrecognized but clinically important contributors to surgical risk.

papers.title: RNAcomp2D: a web tool to execute multiple methods and visually compare predictions of RNA secondary structure.
papers.abstract: Ribonucleic acids (RNAs) are involved in many important biological processes. In particular, non-coding RNAs are crucial regulators of cellular processes, playing a significant role in gene expression. RNA secondary structure is key to infer their specific function and for understanding how they interact with other molecules. Many computational models have been developed in the last decade to predict the secondary structure, achieving increasingly higher success rates. However, each new method has its own input-output interface, programming language, computational requirements and, sometimes,
papers.summary: RNAcomp2D is a web tool that lets users run multiple RNA secondary structure prediction methods through a single interface and visually compare their outputs side by side. It addresses the fragmentation of the field, where each predictor has different inputs, languages, and computational needs, by standardizing execution and visualization. This makes it easier for biologists to benchmark and interpret competing structure predictions without installing or learning each tool.

papers.title: Enhanced prognosis stratification following surgery for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma to optimize clinical decisions by reflecting tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has an extremely dismal postoperative prognosis. Conventional TNM staging cannot adequately characterize tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment, leading to suboptimal risk stratification. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an integrated prognostic system for PDAC by combining deep learning (DL)-based radiomic features with guideline‑recommended clinicopathological variables.
papers.summary: This study develops and externally validates an integrated prognostic system for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) after surgery, combining deep learning-based radiomic features from imaging with standard clinicopathological variables. The goal is to improve risk stratification beyond conventional TNM staging by capturing tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment information that TNM misses. The approach aims to better inform clinical decisions for a cancer with extremely poor postoperative outcomes.

papers.title: Intra-DNA k-mer conservation patterns encode evolutionary selection of variants.
papers.abstract: Current approaches to variant effect prediction center on protein function and interspecies conservation, largely ignoring cues embedded in local nucleotide composition. We developed kGain, a metric that quantifies how a point mutation reshapes oligonucleotide frequency relative to the host genome. In Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae long-term evolution data, fixed, essential-gene, and recurrent mutations carry elevated kGain values that grow more pronounced over successive generations. Parallel trends appear in SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern and in a bottleneck resistance experim
papers.summary: The authors introduce kGain, a metric that measures how a point mutation alters local oligonucleotide (k-mer) frequency relative to the host genome, and show that mutations fixed during long-term evolution in E. coli and yeast, as well as essential-gene and recurrent mutations, carry elevated kGain values that increase over generations. Similar patterns appear in SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern and a bottleneck resistance experiment, suggesting that intra-DNA k-mer conservation encodes a signal of evolutionary selection that is largely independent of protein-level conservation.

papers.title: DNNGP-Pro: A multi-omics data integration platform for predictive modeling of complex traits and crop hybrid breeding.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of complex agronomic traits poses a long-standing challenge for hybrid crop breeding, which may be resolved by integrating multi-omics data with shared-parent relationship information among hybrids. To accelerate variety development, we constructed the DNNGP-Pro platform for predictive modeling of complex hybrid traits in large-scale populations. In preliminary steps, the pipeline extracts local features from omics data via convolutional neural networks, then employs graph convolutional networks to integrate these single-omics features with hybrid shared-parent graph (HSPG)
papers.summary: The authors present DNNGP-Pro, a platform that integrates multi-omics data with shared-parent relationship graphs to predict complex agronomic traits in hybrid crops. It uses convolutional neural networks to extract features from individual omics layers and graph convolutional networks to combine them with hybrid pedigree information, aiming to improve genomic selection for large-scale breeding populations.

papers.title: PRGdb 5.0: a multi-layered resource for plant resistance gene discovery and exploration.
papers.abstract: Plant Resistance Genes database (PRGdb) 5.0 (https://prgdb.org/prgdb5/) is a major update of the PRGdb, designed to expand plant disease resistance gene resources within a unified web platform. The release incorporates predictions for 97 plant proteomes and adds 288, 315 new putative resistance-associated proteins, bringing the database to 874,967 candidate resistance proteins from 279 plant proteomes. The curated reference collection increased from 199 to 462 experimentally supported resistance proteins. To complement domain-based classification, the platform introduces an AI-assisted priorit
papers.summary: PRGdb 5.0 is a major update to the Plant Resistance Genes database, now covering 279 plant proteomes with 874,967 candidate resistance proteins, including 462 experimentally validated ones. It adds AI-assisted prioritization of resistance candidates alongside domain-based classification, providing a unified platform for plant disease resistance gene discovery.

papers.title: Native Mass Spectrometry of Membrane Protein Lipid and Ligand Complexes Using de novo Designed WRAP Domains.
papers.abstract: Membrane proteins engage in dynamic transient interactions with surrounding lipids along with their substrates. Capturing these concomitant contacts often remains a challenging problem. Here, we demonstrate that generative deep learning-designed WRAP domains can preserve weak interactions of membrane proteins in native mass spectrometry. Using WRAP-fused GlpG, AqpM, and OmpA as model systems, we show that lipids can bind in multiple positions inside the WRAP, allowing for their characterization by native mass spectrometry. We show that lipid interactions can be altered by changing the WRAP str
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: The authors show that de novo designed WRAP domains, generated via deep learning, can encapsulate membrane proteins and preserve their weak lipid and ligand interactions for analysis by native mass spectrometry. Using WRAP-fused GlpG, AqpM, and OmpA, they demonstrate that lipids bind at multiple positions within the WRAP and that these interactions can be modulated by altering the WRAP structure. This provides a new strategy for characterizing transient membrane protein–lipid complexes that are typically lost in conventional native MS workflows.

papers.title: Comparing longitudinal regression and deep-learning models for healthcare utilisation prediction: evidence from the SHARE longitudinal panel in Europe.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of outpatient utilisation is essential for health-policy planning, yet work has focused on classical models or deep learning in claims/electronic health record settings. Using longitudinal micro-data from the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe—10 777 adults observed in Waves 5, 6, 8 and 9 (2013, 2015, 2019–2020 and 2021–2022)—we compare classical longitudinal models with sequence-aware neural networks for forecasting Wave 9 outpatient visits from unevenly spaced histories.
papers.summary: This study compares classical longitudinal regression models with sequence-aware neural networks for predicting outpatient healthcare visits using data from 10,777 adults in the SHARE panel across four unevenly spaced waves. It finds that deep learning does not clearly outperform simpler longitudinal models for this prediction task, suggesting that model complexity should be matched to the data structure. The work provides evidence on when sequence-aware neural networks add value in health-policy forecasting.

papers.title: Choroid plexus enlargement in unmedicated major depressive disorder inflammation, oxidative stress and treatment outcome.
papers.abstract: The choroid plexus has emerged as a putative neuroimmune interface implicated in major depressive disorder (MDD). Choroid plexus enlargement has been reported across several MDD cohorts, yet its relationship with peripheral inflammation, oxidative stress, and antidepressant treatment response remains unresolved.
papers.summary: This study examines whether enlargement of the choroid plexus, a brain structure involved in immune-brain communication, is linked to peripheral inflammation, oxidative stress, and antidepressant treatment outcomes in unmedicated patients with major depressive disorder. It aims to clarify the choroid plexus's role as a neuroimmune interface in MDD and whether its size could serve as a marker of treatment response.

papers.title: Multicenter CT-Based Deep Learning for Preoperative Nodal Risk Stratification in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Accurate preoperative risk stratification for lymph node metastasis (LNM) in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) remains difficult. We developed and validated ThyLNT, a Transformer-based 2.5D deep learning model using preoperative computed tomography (CT), and explored related biological features in multi-omics analyses.
papers.journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association
papers.summary: This study developed ThyLNT, a Transformer-based 2.5D deep learning model that uses preoperative CT scans to stratify lymph node metastasis risk in papillary thyroid carcinoma, validated across multiple centers. The authors also linked imaging-derived risk to biological features through multi-omics analyses, aiming to improve preoperative decision-making.

papers.title: Integrated Whole-Cell Phage Display and Machine Learning Identify Candidate Targeting Ligands in KRAS-Defined Lung Cancer Contexts.
papers.abstract: Phage display can identify ligands that target distinctive cell surface phenotypes, but selection outputs are often complex and difficult to interpret. Here, we developed an integrated workflow combining phage display biopanning, next-generation sequencing (NGS), machine learning (ML), and flow cytometry to discover short peptide binders associated with genotype-defined cancer contexts. Phage display was performed on lung cancer cell lines representing KRAS wild-type (WT), G12C, G12D, and G12V backgrounds, and experimental outputs were used to train a multimodal probabilistic model. From the r
papers.summary: The authors combine whole-cell phage display biopanning with next-generation sequencing and machine learning to identify short peptide ligands that distinguish lung cancer cells by KRAS genotype (wild-type, G12C, G12D, G12V). A multimodal probabilistic model trained on the selection outputs prioritizes candidate binders, which are then validated by flow cytometry. The work offers a generalizable pipeline for interpreting complex phage display selections in genotype-defined cancer contexts.

papers.title: Toll-Like Receptors in Mycoplasma Infections: Immunopathogenesis, Cheminformatics, and Machine Learning-Based Insights into TLR-Targeted Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma species are the minimal-genome pathogens that elicit complex host immune responses involving both protective and pathogenic inflammation. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are pivotal components of the immune system, recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and damage-associated molecular patterns to initiate immune responses. TLRs recognize Mycoplasma-derived lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA motifs, initiating NF-κB and MAPK signaling cascades. While these pathways are indispensable for microbial clearance, their dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammation, auto
papers.summary: This review examines how Toll-like receptors recognize Mycoplasma components such as lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA, triggering NF-κB and MAPK signaling that can both clear infection and drive chronic inflammation. The authors combine immunopathogenesis discussion with cheminformatics and machine learning approaches to identify potential TLR-targeted therapeutics. It is a broad synthesis aimed at connecting basic immunology with computational drug discovery for Mycoplasma infections.

papers.title: Large Language Model-Enhanced MFSSG Enables Effective and Accurate Integration Analysis for Microbiome-Metabolome Data.
papers.abstract: The massive volume of paired microbiome and metabolome measurementsgenerated through high-throughput sequencing and mass spectrometryhas created an urgent need for dedicated, integrative analytical pipelines. Existing tools lack the capacity to simultaneously support sample clustering, multi-omics visualization, disease risk stratification, and biological age quantification using matched dual-modal datasets. To overcome this analytical bottleneck, we introduce the matrix factorization with shared and specific graph learning (MFSSG) toolkit: an unsupervised matrix factorization framework that
papers.summary: The authors present MFSSG, a toolkit that combines matrix factorization with shared and specific graph learning to integrate paired microbiome and metabolome data. It is enhanced with a large language model and supports sample clustering, multi-omics visualization, disease risk stratification, and biological age quantification from matched dual-modal datasets. The work addresses the lack of dedicated pipelines for jointly analyzing these two data types.

papers.title: An EFHD1-associated ADSC niche modulates treatment response in experimental models of ER-positive breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) modulate the breast cancer (BC) microenvironment, but their role in endocrine therapy resistance and clinical outcomes remains ill-defined.
papers.summary: This study identifies an EFHD1-associated adipose-derived stem cell (ADSC) niche that influences how ER-positive breast cancer responds to endocrine therapy in experimental models. The findings suggest that ADSCs in the tumor microenvironment contribute to treatment resistance, linking this niche to clinical outcomes.

papers.title: A dendritic cell-related prognostic signature in glioma: A multi-omic framework integrating transcriptomics, single-cell profiling, and clinical validation.
papers.abstract: Dendritic cells (DCs) infiltrating the glioma microenvironment can promote antitumor immunity or contribute to immunosuppression and immune escape. This dual role underscores the need to define dendritic cell-related genes (DCRGs) for prognostic assessment. Using transcriptomic and clinical data from glioma cohorts (The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas (CGGA)), combined with scRNA-seq analysis, we identified ten pivotal DCRGs (CASP1, CD300LF, CTSB, GPR132, HLA-DQA1, PLCB2, RAC2, SIGLEC9, STAT6, TLR1) associated with patient outcomes. A DCRG-based risk signature, devel
papers.summary: The authors combined bulk transcriptomic data from TCGA and CGGA glioma cohorts with single-cell RNA-seq to identify ten dendritic cell-related genes associated with patient survival, and used them to build a prognostic risk signature. The signature stratifies glioma patients by outcome and was validated clinically, highlighting DC-related immune programs in the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important cha
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The paper introduces st2sc, a computational method for recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data. It addresses the challenge of deconvolving spot-level signals into individual cells and accurately estimating per-gene expression, which existing methods have struggled with. This enables more precise single-cell resolution analysis from widely used spatial transcriptomics platforms.

papers.title: Viro-BERT: Whole-genome attention for robust viral pathogen classification from next-generation sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Classifying viral pathogens from next-generation sequencing (NGS) data is central to diagnosis and genomic surveillance. Most deep learning classifiers, however, read only a fixed window at the start of each genome, typically a few hundred to a few thousand base pairs, and so ignore more than 95% of the sequence of large DNA viruses such as monkeypox virus (MPV) and herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1). We refer to this problem as Truncation Blindness. Here we present Viro-BERT, which splits a complete genome into overlapping 512-token windows, encodes each window with a shared DistilBERT encoder, a
papers.summary: Viro-BERT addresses 'Truncation Blindness' in viral pathogen classification by processing entire genomes rather than just a fixed window at the start. It splits complete genomes into overlapping 512-token windows, encodes each with a shared DistilBERT encoder, and aggregates the results to classify viral pathogens from NGS data, enabling use of the full sequence of large DNA viruses like monkeypox and HSV-1.

papers.title: BioLM-Score: Language-Prior Conditioned Probabilistic Geometric Potentials for Protein-Ligand Scoring.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand scoring must address affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening, but these objectives are not necessarily optimized together. Geometric likelihood models may generalize poorly when training-set structural coverage is limited. We test whether pretrained biomolecular representations improve scoring under a controlled geometric baseline.
papers.summary: This paper introduces BioLM-Score, a protein-ligand scoring method that conditions geometric probabilistic potentials on pretrained biomolecular language-model representations. The authors test whether these language priors improve scoring across affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening under a controlled geometric baseline, addressing the concern that purely geometric likelihood models generalize poorly when structural training coverage is limited.

papers.title: Unsupervised Deep Learning for Cryo-EM/ET Particle Classification.
papers.abstract: Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is widely used to determine protein structures from purified samples. With cryogenic electron tomography (cryo-ET), it is possible to image thin sections of cells and directly visualize diverse proteins in their native environment. However, separating the massive mixture of different types of proteins inside cells remains challenging, especially without human intervention. In this work, we present an unsupervised deep learning framework for classifying cryo-EM/ET particle images that jointly optimizes for pose and structure through an autoencoder-based m
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present an unsupervised deep learning framework that classifies cryo-EM and cryo-ET particle images without human intervention by jointly optimizing particle pose and structure through an autoencoder-based model. This addresses the key bottleneck of separating heterogeneous protein mixtures in cellular tomography, enabling automated discovery of distinct protein species in their native environments.

papers.title: Leveraging amino acid embeddings for accurate translation efficiency prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of translation efficiency from mRNA sequences is an important step toward mRNA sequence design. In recent years, the widespread adoption of high-resolution ribosome profiling techniques, such as Ribo-seq, has led to rapid accumulation of large-scale datasets that capture the relationship between mRNA sequences and translation efficiency. This progress has facilitated the development of machine-learning-based models for translation efficiency prediction. However, most existing approaches rely primarily on mRNA-derived features, such as codon usage frequency and 5' untranslat
papers.summary: This paper introduces a machine-learning approach that incorporates amino acid embeddings—learned representations of the protein sequence—to improve prediction of translation efficiency from mRNA sequences. By combining protein-level information with traditional mRNA-derived features like codon usage, the model achieves more accurate predictions than existing methods. This advances the goal of rational mRNA sequence design for therapeutics and biotechnology.

papers.title: Evo2VED: a database of DNA large language model-derived scores for variant interpretation.
papers.abstract: The Evo2 Variant Effect Database (Evo2VED; https://dnallmved.org/) is a publicly accessible resource cataloging precomputed Evo2-derived variant effect scores, defined as allelic score differences, for 6.48 million human variants common in the gnomAD non-Finnish European population. Evo2VED includes scores from the 7B and 40B models under three scoring schemes, alongside annotations of variant function, evolutionary constraint, allele age, and disease associations. It integrates genome-wide association study (GWAS) data from UK Biobank, FinnGen, and the Million Veteran Program. Three complemen
papers.summary: Evo2VED is a public database providing precomputed variant effect scores from the Evo2 DNA large language model (7B and 40B parameter versions, three scoring schemes) for 6.48 million common human variants. It enriches these scores with functional, evolutionary constraint, allele age, and disease association annotations, and integrates GWAS data from UK Biobank, FinnGen, and the Million Veteran Program. This resource enables researchers to interpret genetic variants using LLM-derived predictions without needing to run the models themselves.

papers.title: sorAI - a suite of machine learning models to predict plant polyploidy from target capture data.
papers.abstract: Polyploidy is a persistent feature of land plant evolution, yet it is often difficult to determine the ploidy of individual plants. The growing abundance of target capture data and other high throughput sequence datasets across plant species has generated interest in methods to infer ploidy from these data. We leverage chromosome count data and target capture data from the GoFlag probe set in ferns to train new machine learning models to infer if a sample is from a diploid or polyploid genome.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed sorAI, a suite of machine learning models that predict whether a plant sample is diploid or polyploid using target capture sequencing data. They trained the models on chromosome count data and GoFlag probe set data from ferns, addressing the common difficulty of determining ploidy in individual plants. This provides a new computational approach to infer ploidy from the growing volume of high-throughput sequence data in plants.

papers.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase d
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint benchmarks protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction methods on their ability to predict how mutations in the MET kinase affect inhibitor responses, using deep mutational scanning data across 11 inhibitor conditions. The authors find that these models struggle to generalize to mutation-dependent drug responses, highlighting limitations in current computational drug discovery approaches. The work provides a systematic evaluation framework for assessing model performance on mutation-drug interaction prediction tasks.

papers.title: LLM Representations Rival Traditional Predictors and Enhance Multimodal Prediction of APOE4 and Aβ-Burden.
papers.abstract: Spontaneous language offers a scalable, non-invasive approach for identifying biological indicators of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD). We examined prediction of APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-β (Aβ) burden using Cookie Theft picture-descriptions from two cohorts, including Hebrew- and English-speakers (IRAP, N=134; and WRAP, N=1,541). Aβ burden was classified across lowest-quartile, median, and highest-quartile cutoffs, capturing accumulation below conventional amyloid-positivity thresholds. We compared embeddings from pretrained large language models (LLMs) to standard cognit
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study shows that language embeddings from pretrained large language models can predict APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-β burden from spontaneous speech (Cookie Theft picture descriptions) as well as or better than traditional cognitive predictors, across Hebrew- and English-speaking cohorts. Combining LLM representations with standard predictors improved multimodal prediction, including at sub-threshold amyloid cutoffs relevant to preclinical Alzheimer's disease.

papers.title: Unraveling the genetic architecture of the human mammillary bodies.
papers.abstract: The mammillary bodies are a central component of the hippocampal-diencephalic-cingulate network that is critically involved in emotion processing and memory function, yet their genetic architecture remains unknown. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of mammillary body volume in 38,064 participants from the UK Biobank and replicated our findings in the Rhineland Study cohort (N = 4,860). Mammillary body and hypothalamic subregional volumes were derived from structural brain MRIs using FastSurfer-HypVINN, an established and validated deep learning-based segmentation tool. Univar
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study performed the first genome-wide association study of mammillary body volume, a brain structure important for memory and emotion, using MRI data from over 38,000 UK Biobank participants with replication in a German cohort. The authors used a deep learning segmentation tool to measure hypothalamic subregions and identified genetic variants associated with mammillary body volume. This establishes a genetic basis for individual differences in this understudied brain structure.

papers.title: A Hybrid Ligand- and Structure-Based Drug Design Invoked through Square Attention in Protein-Ligand Transformer.
papers.abstract: Computer-aided molecular design based on evaluation of protein-ligand (PL) binding affinity is important for accelerating drug discovery. A deep-learning model for natural language processing (NLP) involving an attention mechanism (i.e., Transformer) is expected to improve the PL-affinity evaluation along with clarifying amino acid residues and ligand atoms that are responsible for molecular interactions. However, the original attention (i.e., a scaled dot-product with row-wise Softmax normalization) is an adapted method for relationships between homogeneous inputs (e.g., two sentences in the
papers.summary: The authors introduce a 'square attention' mechanism for a protein-ligand Transformer that replaces the standard row-wise Softmax normalization, enabling the model to jointly leverage ligand-based and structure-based information for binding-affinity prediction. This hybrid approach is intended to improve affinity evaluation while also identifying the amino acid residues and ligand atoms driving molecular interactions. The work targets computer-aided drug design by combining the interpretability of attention with both ligand and structural inputs.

papers.title: HMB-Net: Synergizing Latent Sequential Dynamics and Local Sequence Motifs for Robust RNA Methylation Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate site-level identification of RNA post-transcriptional modifications is essential for deciphering epitranscriptomic regulation. However, existing deep learning predictors typically rely on either convolutional filters with limited receptive fields or self-attention mechanisms with quadratic complexity, while parallel hybrid networks often struggle to coordinate global sequence context with local motif sensitivity. Here, we present HMB-Net, an interpretable hybrid framework that couples a Selective State Space Model (Mamba) with a deep Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) netw
papers.summary: HMB-Net is a deep learning framework for predicting RNA methylation sites that combines a Mamba selective state space model (for efficient long-range sequence context) with a Bi-LSTM network (for local motif sensitivity). The hybrid design aims to overcome the limited receptive fields of CNNs and the quadratic cost of self-attention while better coordinating global and local sequence information. The work is presented as an interpretable predictor for site-level epitranscriptomic modification identification.

papers.title: stem.MAP: Identification of cell-type-specific protein complexes in mammalian embryonic stem cells.
papers.abstract: Protein complexes carry out critical functions during development. Mapping cell-type-specific protein complexes in early embryogenesis is essential for uncovering the molecular mechanisms of embryonic development. We unfortunately currently lack a catalog of protein complexes specific for embryogenesis including embryonic stem cells. Here we develop a proteomics-based machine learning workflow to predict protein complexes present in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESC). Our method integrates data from a cell-type agnostic protein complex resource with co-fractionation mass spectrometry (CF-MS) ex
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed stem.MAP, a proteomics-based machine learning workflow that integrates existing protein complex data with co-fractionation mass spectrometry to predict cell-type-specific protein complexes in mouse embryonic stem cells. This provides a first catalog of protein complexes specific to early embryogenesis and ESCs, addressing a gap in developmental biology resources.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Protein-Ligand Binding Site Prediction from Protein Sequence and SMILES.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of protein-ligand binding sites is critical for mechanistic biology and drug discovery, yet predictive performance varies substantially across ligand families and data-availability regimes. We present a systematic ligand-aware benchmark and evaluation framework for residue-level binding-site prediction across three settings: overrepresented ligands with abundant examples, underrepresented ligands with limited examples, and zero-shot ligands unseen during training. Using a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering, we evaluate a progressive three-s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a ligand-aware benchmark for predicting protein-ligand binding sites at residue resolution, evaluating models across three regimes: ligands with abundant training data, underrepresented ligands, and zero-shot ligands never seen during training. The framework uses a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering and a progressive three-stage evaluation, revealing how predictive performance degrades as ligand data availability decreases.

papers.title: GAC-BiT-CNN: A Hybrid Generative Adversarial Capsule-Transformer-CNN Model with Fused Protein Language Model Embeddings for Methyltransferase Prediction.
papers.abstract: Methyltransferases (MTs) are a functionally diverse class of enzymes that catalyse methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) to DNA, RNA, and proteins, thereby regulating epigenetic programming, gene expression, and numerous disease processes. Dysregulation of these enzymes is implicated in a wide spectrum of human cancers and neurodegenerative disorders, making their accurate computational identification a priority in both basic research and drug discovery. We present GAC-BiT-CNN, a novel hybrid deep learning framework integrating Generative Adversarial Capsule Networks (GAC),
papers.summary: The authors present GAC-BiT-CNN, a hybrid deep learning framework that combines generative adversarial capsule networks, a bidirectional transformer, and a CNN, using fused protein language model embeddings to predict methyltransferase enzymes from sequence. The model aims to improve computational identification of this epigenetically important enzyme class, which is implicated in cancer and neurodegenerative disease.

papers.title: Protify: A Benchmarking Platform Revealing Task Dependence and Homology Leakage in Protein Language Model Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Protein Language Models (pLMs) have become essential tools for computational protein analysis, and the rapid proliferation of architectures, training objectives, and pretraining corpora has produced a diverse and expanding model landscape. Evaluation practices, however, remain fragmented: studies use different datasets, preprocessing pipelines, and reporting conventions, so results rarely transfer between publications. Here we introduce Protify, an open-source platform that standardizes pLM benchmarking across zero-shot, supervised, and transfer-learning settings through a unified, low-code in
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Protify is an open-source benchmarking platform that standardizes evaluation of protein language models across zero-shot, supervised, and transfer-learning settings using a unified low-code interface. The platform reveals that model performance is highly task-dependent and that homology leakage between pretraining and evaluation data can inflate benchmark results, highlighting the need for standardized, leakage-aware evaluation practices.

papers.title: A protein language model for domain, functional site, and variant effect prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein sequence databases are growing far faster than experimentally curated annotations, limiting functional interpretation of newly identified proteins and coding variants. We developed PALM, a protein annotation language model that jointly predicts domain and functional-site occurrence, while preserving overlapping and nested annotations through a soft-target objective. PALM integrates ESM2 with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), learned layer aggregation, and a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) encoder. PALM was trained on ∼15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences spanning 17
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present PALM, a protein language model that combines ESM2 embeddings with LoRA fine-tuning, learned layer aggregation, and a BiLSTM encoder to jointly predict protein domains and functional sites. A soft-target objective allows PALM to preserve overlapping and nested annotations, which is important because domains and sites frequently co-occur. Trained on ~15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences, PALM also extends to variant effect prediction, addressing the gap between rapidly growing sequence databases and slow experimental annotation.

papers.title: AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free enrichment reveal tumor heterogeneity, genomic relatedness, and divergence in malignant effusions.
papers.abstract: Malignant effusions are clinically accessible yet underutilized sources of metastatic tumor cells. However, abundant background immune cells complicate tumor cell isolation and molecular characterization. We integrate AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free tumor cell enrichment with genomic profiling to characterize phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity in malignant effusions.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint describes an integrated workflow combining AI-powered single-cell imaging with morphology-guided, label-free enrichment to isolate tumor cells from malignant effusions, which are typically dominated by background immune cells. The enriched cells are then genomically profiled, revealing tumor heterogeneity, genomic relatedness, and divergence among metastatic populations. The approach highlights effusions as an underused but accessible source of metastatic tumor cells for molecular characterization.

papers.title: Synthetic MPRA perturbation supervision improves variant-effect prediction in sequence-to-function models.
papers.abstract: Deep learning sequence-to-function (S2F) models learn to predict functional readouts, such as gene expression, from genetic sequence. However, these models are trained predominantly on the reference genome and struggle to accurately predict the effect of genetic variation on gene expression. Massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) explore the direct impact of genetic variation on gene expression, but saturation-mutagenesis MPRAs that measure variant effects directly remain limited, thereby restricting their use for fine-tuning S2F models. In this work, we investigate fine-tuning Borzoi, a s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors show that fine-tuning the sequence-to-function model Borzoi on synthetic MPRA perturbation data improves its ability to predict the effects of genetic variants on gene expression. Because real saturation-mutagenesis MPRA data are scarce, they generate synthetic perturbation supervision to bridge the gap between reference-genome training and variant-effect prediction. This offers a practical route to better variant-effect models without requiring large experimental MPRA datasets.

papers.title: Predicting single-molecule chromatin distribution from DNA sequence.
papers.abstract: Genome regulation unfolds through dynamic and stochastic single-molecule events. Deep learning models that read gene regulatory activities from DNA sequences have markedly advanced our ability to predict cell-population-level averages. However, they cannot capture the full spectrum of heterogeneity and dynamics at the single-molecule level, which directly reflect the underlying mechanisms of genome regulation. Here, we introduce a sequence-to-distribution (S2d) framework that directly models the entire probabilistic distribution of single-molecule chromatin states from DNA sequence alone. We u
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a sequence-to-distribution (S2d) deep learning framework that predicts the full probabilistic distribution of single-molecule chromatin states directly from DNA sequence, rather than only population-level averages. This enables modeling of the heterogeneity and stochastic dynamics of genome regulation that conventional sequence-to-activity models cannot capture.

papers.title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq.
papers.abstract: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. VIGAT jointly examines accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes, integrating genomic annotations and biological context to select gene-specific regions enriched for cluster-di
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: VIGAT is a new tool that uses a vision-language model to automatically interpret ATAC-seq coverage plots and adaptively quantify gene activity from single-cell ATAC-seq data. By jointly examining accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes and integrating genomic annotations, it selects gene-specific regions that better discriminate cell types. This addresses the challenge that informative regulatory regions vary across genes and tissues, improving gene activity quantification.

papers.title: Computational immunogenicity prediction for mRNA vaccines: benchmarks, bottlenecks, and the peptide-nucleotide gap.
papers.abstract: Computational prediction of T-cell epitopes has become indispensable to vaccine design, yet the field still relies on the assumption that how much of a given antigen is produced is fixed by its coding sequence. However, this is not the case with mRNA vaccines, i.e. the design of the mRNA template can vastly alter the quantity of the same protein produced. Codon usage, guanine-cytosine (GC) content, untranslated-region (UTR) design, and predicted secondary structure together define how fast the message is translated and how long it survives, and therefore how much antigen ever reaches the prese
papers.summary: This review argues that computational T-cell epitope prediction for mRNA vaccines is limited by a key blind spot: existing tools assume antigen production is fixed by the coding sequence, but mRNA design choices (codon usage, GC content, UTRs, secondary structure) strongly modulate how much protein is actually made. The authors benchmark current immunogenicity predictors and identify bottlenecks, framing the 'peptide-nucleotide gap' as a central obstacle to reliable vaccine design.

papers.title: Transformer models in genomics: from sequence analysis to population genetics and biodiversity.
papers.abstract: Modern genomics and artificial intelligence converge at a breakthrough point with the emergence of transformer-based large language models for genomic analysis. This review examines how transformer-based models have advanced genomic sequence analysis through novel tokenization strategies, self-attention mechanisms, and pre-training/fine-tuning paradigms. Unlike prior broad surveys, we focus on three sub-areas of genomics where transformer architectures have had a substantive impact: sequence-level analysis, population-level genetics, including genetic imputation and genome-wide association ana
papers.summary: This review examines how transformer-based models are being applied to genomic sequence analysis, focusing on tokenization strategies, self-attention mechanisms, and pre-training/fine-tuning approaches. It highlights three areas where these architectures have had substantive impact: sequence-level analysis, population genetics (including genetic imputation and GWAS), and biodiversity. The paper provides a focused survey of the intersection between large language models and genomics.

papers.title: Interaction-finder: automated literature-based discovery of biological entity associations with quote-level provenance.
papers.abstract: Identifying interactions between biological entities is a cornerstone of molecular research, but assembling such lists from the literature is slow and tedious. For many research questions, no curated database exists, leaving researchers to survey the relevant literature themselves. We present interaction-finder, a tool that automates this process: given a topic string and user-defined entity types, it discovers relevant literature through LLM-guided iterative search, extracts candidate associations from full-text articles, and produces a ranked list where every association is backed by quoted
papers.summary: The authors present interaction-finder, a tool that automates literature-based discovery of associations between biological entities. Given a topic and user-defined entity types, it uses LLM-guided iterative search to find relevant full-text articles, extracts candidate associations, and returns a ranked list where each association is supported by quoted evidence. This addresses the gap where no curated database exists and researchers must manually survey literature.

papers.title: Handshake: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction at scale using ProstT5 and cross-chain attention.
papers.abstract: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction, identifying which residues of a protein form the interface when bound to a specific partner, remains a challenging task with significant implications for drug discovery and understanding of protein structure and function. Existing computational methods are limited by small training datasets, inconsistent redundancy filtering, and reliance on three-dimensional structural information at test time. Here we present a sequence-only, partner-specific protein-protein interface predictor called HandShake. It combines ProstT5, a protein language
papers.summary: HandShake is a sequence-only computational tool that predicts which residues of a protein form the binding interface with a specific partner, using the ProstT5 protein language model and cross-chain attention. It addresses limitations of prior methods by training on a larger, consistently filtered dataset and requiring no 3D structural information at test time. This enables partner-specific interface prediction at scale, with implications for drug discovery and protein function analysis.

papers.title: Transductive Learning From a Transformer Foundation Model Improves the Taxonomic Classification of eDNA Metabarcodes.
papers.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a powerful and cost-effective biodiversity monitoring tool, providing comprehensive and non-invasive taxonomic inventories. However, eDNA-based monitoring is strongly dependent on the completeness of genetic reference databases, which varies greatly among regions and taxa. Since completing gaps at the species level is unrealistic in the short term, an alternative is to infer coarser taxonomic assignments for sequences belonging to species not yet in reference databases. To address this challenge, we introduce BouillaBERT, a novel deep learning method tai
papers.summary: The authors introduce BouillaBERT, a deep learning method that uses a transformer foundation model with transductive learning to classify eDNA metabarcodes taxonomically. This approach aims to improve taxonomic assignment for species missing from incomplete reference databases by inferring coarser taxonomic levels, addressing a major limitation in eDNA-based biodiversity monitoring.

papers.title: An antigen-specific protein language model guides CDR optimization for antibody design.
papers.abstract: The capacity of an antibody to recognize and bind an antigen with high specificity and strength (i.e., its binding affinity) is a key determinant in the design and optimization of neutralizing antibodies against pathogenic targets. Here we introduce Ab-Affinity, a fine-tuned protein language model (PLM) that predicts the binding affinity of an antibody against a target peptide within the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. Cross-validation results shows that Ab-Affinity outperforms other PLM-based affinity predictors when evaluated on a held-out validation and independent test sets. When integrated with
papers.summary: The authors present Ab-Affinity, a fine-tuned protein language model that predicts antibody-antigen binding affinity specifically for targets within the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. In cross-validation, it outperforms other PLM-based affinity predictors on held-out and independent test sets, and it is integrated into a workflow to guide optimization of antibody complementarity-determining regions (CDRs).

papers.title: A Transformers Analysis Pipeline (TrAP) to Evaluate LINE-1 RNA Sequence Content.
papers.abstract: LINE-1 RNA has emerged as a potential regulator of chromatin organization and gene expression, as well as a candidate readout of cellular and disease-associated states. Accurate measurement of LINE-1 transcript abundance is therefore important for evaluating its regulatory, biomarker, and potential therapeutic relevance. Measurement is challenging in short-read RNA sequencing because similar LINE-1 loci produce ambiguous, multi-mapping reads and LINE-1-associated signal can arise from passive as well as autonomous transcription. We developed the Transformers Analysis Pipeline (TrAP), an alignm
papers.summary: The authors present TrAP, a bioinformatics pipeline that uses transformer-based machine learning to analyze LINE-1 RNA sequences from short-read RNA sequencing data. The tool addresses the challenge of multi-mapping reads from highly similar LINE-1 loci, aiming to improve accurate measurement of LINE-1 transcript abundance for studies of chromatin regulation and disease biomarkers.

papers.title: HierL2GDTA: Hierarchical Interaction Modeling with Local and Global Features for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target binding affinity is essential for drug discovery. However, existing methods face limitations in capturing local and global molecular features and in effectively integrating protein and ligand representations for interaction modeling. Here, we present HierL2GDTA, a sequence-based hierarchical framework for predicting binding affinity. Pretrained protein and molecular representations are processed by multi-scale convolutions to extract local features, followed by a bidirectional gated recurrent unit and dilated convolutions to capture broader protein and ligand
papers.summary: HierL2GDTA is a sequence-based deep learning framework for predicting drug-target binding affinity that combines pretrained protein and molecular representations with multi-scale convolutions for local feature extraction and bidirectional GRU plus dilated convolutions for broader context. The hierarchical design aims to better integrate ligand and protein representations for interaction modeling, addressing limitations of prior methods in capturing both local and global molecular features.

papers.title: LLM-Guided Adaptive Cost Calibration in Active Learning for Parkinson's Disease Biosignals.
papers.abstract: Confirmatory labels for Parkinson's disease (PD), from expert examination or, prospectively, biological assays, are costly, and missed cases and false alarms carry unequal consequences. ClinRisk-LLM is a framework for label-efficient, cost-aware learning from gait and speech signals in which a large language model (LLM) translates a predefined safety specification into a frozen policy setting the positive-class weight of a support vector machine and the priority of potential missed cases for annotation. Cost-sensitive training, risk-aware querying and the LLM policy were ablated on gait (n=165
papers.summary: The authors present ClinRisk-LLM, a framework that uses a large language model to set cost-sensitive learning parameters and prioritize which unlabeled Parkinson's disease biosignal samples (gait and speech) should be annotated, aiming to reduce labeling cost while accounting for the unequal consequences of missed cases versus false alarms. Ablation experiments on gait data (n=165) evaluate the contributions of cost-sensitive training, risk-aware querying, and the LLM-derived policy.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Precision Nanomedicine: Bridging Delivery Barriers, Controlled Release, and Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Targeted drug delivery aims to enhance therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity, yet its clinical translation remains limited by the unpredictable in vivo behaviour of nanocarriers. Although a broad range of nanocarrier platforms-including lipid-, polymer-, protein-, inorganic- and biomimetic-based systems-can improve drug solubility, pharmacokinetics, lesion-site accumulation and controlled release, their performance is frequently constrained by heterogeneous disease biology, insufficient tissue penetration, premature clearance, immune recognition and manufacturing variability.
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence can guide the design and clinical translation of nanomedicine drug delivery systems. It argues that while many nanocarrier platforms can improve drug solubility, pharmacokinetics, and targeted accumulation, their clinical success is limited by unpredictable in vivo behavior, heterogeneous disease biology, immune recognition, and manufacturing variability—challenges that AI could help address by optimizing delivery barriers and controlled release.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics, machine learning, computational toxicology, and experimental validation reveal PFAS-associated immune-inflammatory signatures in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants increasingly implicated in respiratory disorders. However, the systems-level connections among PFAS-associated molecular perturbations, immune dysregulation, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain poorly understood. This study aimed to prioritize candidate links between PFAS-associated target information and COPD-related transcriptional and inflammatory signatures.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data, machine learning, computational toxicology, and experimental validation to identify molecular connections between PFAS exposure and COPD. The authors prioritize candidate PFAS-associated targets that overlap with COPD-related transcriptional and inflammatory signatures, highlighting immune-inflammatory pathways as potential mediators. Experimental validation supports these computational predictions, suggesting PFAS may contribute to COPD pathogenesis through immune dysregulation.

papers.title: Physiological proxies of feed efficiency in pigs: exploring the predictive value of blood biochemical and hematological profiles.
papers.abstract: Developing strategies to improve feed efficiency can help the swine industry become more sustainable while meeting the worldwide demand for pork products, yet most commercial barns cannot practically calculate direct metrics of individual feed efficiency. Physiological indicators of metabolic pathways can serve as intermediate variables to predict performance outcomes and, therefore, as biomarkers of feed efficiency and other desirable production traits in growing pigs. This research aimed to assess the role of conventional blood parameters as proxies for performance outcomes and their predict
papers.summary: This study tested whether routine blood biochemical and hematological measurements can serve as practical proxies for feed efficiency in growing pigs, since direct measurement of individual feed intake is impractical in commercial barns. The authors assessed conventional blood parameters as intermediate physiological indicators and evaluated their predictive value for performance outcomes. The work supports using accessible blood profiles as biomarkers to indirectly identify more feed-efficient animals.

papers.title: A Machine-Learning Framework Integrating Frequency-Domain Spectral Features for Ligand Classification and Candidate Prioritization.
papers.abstract: AI-assisted drug discovery (AIDD) combines molecular modeling with machine learning to support lead identification and candidate prioritization. Conventional molecular descriptors principally encode static chemical structures, leaving frequency-domain behavior as an additional source of molecular information. We therefore developed the terahertz fusion descriptor (THz-FD), a feature-fusion framework that integrates terahertz (THz) frequency-domain features for Na+/K+-ATPase ligand classification and retrospective ranking. Extra Trees (ET), Random Forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) c
papers.summary: The authors introduce THz-FD, a feature-fusion framework that combines conventional molecular descriptors with terahertz frequency-domain spectral features to classify Na+/K+-ATPase ligands and prioritize candidates. Using Extra Trees, Random Forest, and SVM classifiers, they show that adding frequency-domain information can improve ligand classification and retrospective ranking. The work suggests spectral behavior is an underexploited source of molecular information for AI-assisted drug discovery.

papers.title: Integrative ferroptosis-related bioinformatics identifies PPARγ as a therapeutic target of ursolic acid against inflammation and pathological osteogenesis in ankylosing spondylitis.
papers.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disease characterized by persistent inflammation and aberrant new bone formation. Ferroptosis has increasingly been implicated in immune dysregulation and pathological bone remodeling; however, its molecular involvement in AS and its potential value for natural product discovery remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify ferroptosis-related molecular targets in AS, screen natural compounds targeting the key candidate, and validate their therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates ferroptosis-related bioinformatics with natural product screening to identify PPARγ as a key target in ankylosing spondylitis, a chronic inflammatory disease involving abnormal bone formation. The authors show that ursolic acid, a natural compound, acts on PPARγ to reduce inflammation and pathological osteogenesis, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for AS.

papers.title: Medical-oriented multi-label diagnosis of twelve-lead ECG signals via disease-aware relational modeling and pathology-aware temporal evidence aggregation.
papers.abstract: Twelve-lead ECG signals are of great value in cardiovascular disease screening and assisted diagnosis, but their multi-label recognition process is simultaneously affected by cross-lead structural dependencies, disease label co-occurrence relationships, and the dispersed distribution of pathological evidence in long-sequence signals. To address these issues, this study proposes a deep learning model for twelve-lead ECG multi-label diagnosis. The model adopts a Transformer-Mamba hybrid structure as the temporal encoding backbone to extract local waveform variations and long-range rhythm feature
papers.summary: This paper proposes a deep learning model for multi-label diagnosis from twelve-lead ECG signals that combines a Transformer-Mamba hybrid temporal encoder with disease-aware relational modeling and pathology-aware evidence aggregation. The approach is designed to capture cross-lead structural dependencies, label co-occurrence patterns, and dispersed pathological evidence across long sequences. It is a methodological contribution aimed at improving automated cardiovascular screening.

papers.title: Machine learning prediction of 1-year thrombosis risk in membranous nephropathy: integration of renal pathology and early longitudinal trajectories.
papers.abstract: Patients with membranous nephropathy (MN) have an increased risk of thrombotic events. Existing prediction approaches primarily use clinical and laboratory measurements obtained at a single time point and rarely incorporate renal pathology or early longitudinal changes. This study integrated multiple types of information to predict the occurrence of thrombosis from 4 weeks after discharge to 1 year after being diagnosed with MN.
papers.summary: This study develops a machine learning model to predict the risk of thrombotic events within one year of diagnosis for patients with membranous nephropathy. Unlike prior approaches that rely on single-timepoint clinical labs, the model integrates renal pathology features with early longitudinal trajectories of clinical measurements. The work aims to improve risk stratification for a known complication of MN.

papers.title: A machine learning-assisted hypoxia-associated prognostic model reveals PFKP-mediated glycolytic regulation in uveal melanoma.
papers.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is a highly aggressive intraocular malignancy with strong metastatic propensity and poor response to immunotherapy. Hypoxia profoundly reshapes the tumor microenvironment and drives immune evasion. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-assisted hypoxia-related prognostic model and identify relevant metabolic candidates associated with UM progression.
papers.summary: The authors built a machine-learning prognostic model for uveal melanoma based on hypoxia-related genes, and identified PFKP, a glycolytic enzyme, as a candidate driving tumor progression. The work links hypoxia and glycolytic metabolism to immune microenvironment remodeling in this aggressive eye cancer, though the findings are primarily computational and need experimental validation.

papers.title: Predicting Translation Readthrough from Sequence Features in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.abstract: Understanding translation readthrough in eukaryotes is fundamental for elucidating transcript evolution, deciphering gene expression codes, and advancing biotechnological applications. In this study, we present the first comprehensive analysis of the transcript features that determine readthrough efficiency in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. To predict readthrough efficiency, we engineered a set of novel sequence-derived features and trained multiple machine learning models, achieving a mean Spearman correlation of 0.535 between predicted and experimentally measured values, substantially improving p
papers.summary: This study identifies transcript sequence features that determine how often ribosomes fail to stop at a stop codon (translation readthrough) in yeast. The authors engineered novel sequence-derived features and trained machine learning models that predict readthrough efficiency with a mean Spearman correlation of 0.535, substantially outperforming prior approaches. This is the first comprehensive analysis of readthrough determinants in S. cerevisiae.

papers.title: Prediction of multi-stage Alzheimer's disease progression based on surface-based morphometry and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Early identification of individuals at high risk of progression from normal cognition (NC) to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and from MCI to Alzheimer's disease (AD) is crucial for timely intervention. However, predictive models that simultaneously address multiple transition stages along the AD continuum remain limited.
papers.summary: This study develops machine learning models that use surface-based morphometry (cortical thickness, surface area, and curvature measures from structural MRI) to predict transitions along the Alzheimer's disease continuum—from normal cognition to mild cognitive impairment and from MCI to Alzheimer's disease. By modeling multiple transition stages simultaneously rather than a single binary outcome, the work aims to improve early identification of individuals at high risk of progression.

papers.title: Explainable volumetric deep learning from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI for preoperative IDH prediction in adult-type diffuse gliomas: a two-center study.
papers.abstract: To evaluate contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI (CE-T1WI) models for preoperative prediction of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status in adult-type diffuse gliomas and explore phenotype associations of influential latent features.
papers.summary: This two-center study develops explainable volumetric deep learning models using contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI to preoperatively predict IDH mutation status in adult-type diffuse gliomas. The authors also investigate phenotype associations of the latent features driving model predictions, aiming to make the deep learning outputs more interpretable for clinical use.

papers.title: Macronutrient composition and incident hypertension during China's nutrition transition: a longitudinal cohort analysis of the China Health and Nutrition Survey.
papers.abstract: China's nutrition transition has shifted dietary macronutrient composition while hypertension prevalence has risen. Whether the routinely available macronutrient composition adequately captures the risk of incident hypertension remains unclear.
papers.summary: This longitudinal cohort analysis uses China Health and Nutrition Survey data to examine whether dietary macronutrient composition predicts incident hypertension during China's nutrition transition. The abstract does not report specific findings, so the direction and magnitude of any association remain unclear from the available text.

papers.title: ToxiFusion: integrating contextual and compositional sequence representations for toxic peptide prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting of toxic peptides from sequence information is important for peptide safety assessment and therapeutic development. However, reported performance of computational predictors can be affected by representation limitations and evaluation bias.
papers.summary: ToxiFusion introduces a computational method for predicting toxic peptides directly from their amino acid sequences by combining contextual and compositional sequence representations. The authors highlight that existing predictors suffer from representation limitations and evaluation bias, and propose their integrated approach to improve accuracy. This work aims to support peptide safety assessment and therapeutic development.
